# QR Code third-party code

- Runtime encoder: [qrcode-generator](https://github.com/kazuhikoarase/qrcode-generator), **2.0.4**, Kazuhiko Arase, MIT. Distributed source: `https://registry.npmjs.org/qrcode-generator/-/qrcode-generator-2.0.4.tgz`, `package/dist/qrcode.js`, copied verbatim as `qrcode-generator-2.0.4.js` (56,694 bytes). SHA-256: `79ec86f82856005b1c887905cfccfcfbec3821ca61c7fd5a952faa5f778f791c`. Copyright/header preserved; MIT terms in `qrcode-generator-LICENSE.txt`.
- Independent test decoder: [jsQR](https://github.com/cozmo/jsQR), **1.4.0**, Apache-2.0, pinned in package-lock.json. Development/test only; not shipped to visitors. Its distribution includes its license in node_modules/jsqr/LICENSE.
- Review: inspected the distributed encoder for network requests, dynamic code execution and DOM writes. It has no fetch/XHR, eval or document access. HTML/SVG string helpers exist but are unused. We use only Byte-mode encoding/matrix access, draw black/white canvas with four modules of quiet zone, and serialize PNG. The input is restricted to the existing canonical HTTPS station link on this project's production origin/path; no GPS or private preferences. Independent decoding verifies the payload byte for byte. This inspection is not a formal security certification.
- No QR API/CDN. Encoder loads from the project path only when requested (the existing PWA also verifies/caches this static interface asset during installation). jsQR never runs on the public website. Preserve notices and hashes when upgrading; rerun QR, PWA and browser tests.
